hypotheses: nu > 0 is an arbitrary positive viscosity
preamble_entries.conclusion: There exist a force f in C_c^infty(R^3 x (0,infty); R^3), a compact set K subset R^3, and smooth velocity and pressure fields u, p on R^3 x [0,1) solving d_t u + (u.grad)u - nu Laplacian u + grad p = f, div u = 0, u(.,0) = 0 (1.1), such that supp u(.,t) union supp p(.,t) subset K for every 0 <= t < 1, sup_{0<=t<1} ||u(t)||_{L^2(R^3)} < infty, and limsup_{t->1} ||u(t)||_{L^infty(R^3)} = infty. Consequently there is no smooth solution (u,P) on R^3 x [0,infty) with the same force and initial datum whose kinetic energy sup_{t>=0} (1/2) int |u|^2 is uniformly bounded. (Stated as establishing alternative (C) of the Millennium problem statement [13]; the periodic alternative (D) is Corollary 10.6.)
constants: A = 1/2 + h, D = 1/2 - h, 0 < h < 1/100 (from Section 3)
growth path x_tau = (sqrt(2 X_in tau), 0, 0), t = 1 - tau (10.20), with X_in in (0, X_a) fixed in Theorem 3.1(iv)
u_theta(x_tau, 1 - tau) = tau^{-A}(e_0 + O(tau^{2h})) -> +infty (10.21), e_0 > 0
viscosity rescaling (10.22): u_nu(x,t) = sqrt(nu) u(x/sqrt(nu), t), p_nu = nu p(x/sqrt(nu), t), f_nu = sqrt(nu) f(x/sqrt(nu), t); singular time unchanged
rescaled support K_nu = sqrt(nu) K; force support K_nu x [0,2]
derivative scaling d^alpha_x d^m_t f_nu = nu^{(1-|alpha|)/2} (d^alpha_y d^m_t f)(x/sqrt(nu), t)
competitor rescaling v(y,t) = nu^{-1/2} v_nu(sqrt(nu) y, t), P = nu^{-1} P_nu(sqrt(nu) y, t), ||v||_2^2 = nu^{-5/2} ||v_nu||_2^2
regularity class used: u in C([0,T]; H^3) for each T < 1
cites: Sobolev embedding H^3(R^3) into L^infty(R^3) and H^3 into W^{1,infty}
preamble_entries.role: Main theorem: a smooth compactly supported force drives a zero-datum bounded-energy Navier-Stokes flow to unbounded velocity at time 1, excluding any global smooth bounded-energy solution; proved on p. 124 by combining the localized fields (Prop 10.1, Lemmas 10.3-10.5) with the inner growth (3.6) of Theorem 3.1 and the viscosity rescaling (10.22).

hypotheses: None beyond the existence of the stated constants: it asserts that there are constants 0 < h < 1/100, q_* > 0, 0 < X_a < X_ext < infty and smooth fields (u,p) on Omega_* = {(x,t): tau > 0, q < q_*} (viscosity one, residual R of (3.1))
Coordinates: tau = 1 - t, q = q(z,t) defined by tau = q(1 - eta^2), z = q^D eta, X = r^2/(2q) (3.2)
preamble_entries.conclusion: (i) u = curl A + B e_theta (3.3) with A a vector potential and B an axisymmetric scalar; A and B e_theta smooth in Cartesian coordinates at the axis; u exactly divergence-free. (ii) Every Cartesian space-time derivative of A, B e_theta, p is uniformly bounded on compact spatial subsets with c <= q <= c' < q_*, for each 0 < c < c', up to the one-sided boundary tau = 0, with the derivative limits compatible under spatial and time differentiation. (iii) For every alpha, b, N and finite X_1: |d^alpha_x d^b_t R(u,p)| <= C_{alpha,b,N,X_1} q^N on 0 <= X <= X_1 as q -> 0 (3.4); for X >= X_ext the residual is identically zero and A = 0, B = K(r,tau), p = -int_r^infty K(rho,tau)^2/rho d rho, K(r,tau) = r^{-1-2h} H_ext(tau/r^2) (3.5), with H_ext smooth on [0,infty) with each fixed derivative bounded, and K solving the radial swirl heat equation -d_tau K = d_r^2 K + r^{-1} d_r K - r^{-2} K. (iv) For some fixed X_in in (0, X_a) and e_0 > 0: u_theta(sqrt(2 X_in tau), 0, 0, 1 - tau) = tau^{-A}(e_0 + O(tau^{2h})) as tau -> 0 (3.6).
constants: q_* > 0 (later taken equal to q_big of Lemma 9.7)
0 < X_a < X_ext < infty; X_in in (0, X_a); e_0 > 0
Omega_* = {tau > 0, q < q_*}
K(r,tau) = r^{-1-2h} H_ext(tau/r^2); exterior pressure -int_r^infty K^2/rho d rho
swirl heat equation -d_tau K = d_r^2 K + r^{-1} d_r K - r^{-2} K
preamble_entries.role: The local existence theorem: it packages the local field (u_loc, p_loc) with its potential representation, one-sided endpoint regularity, flat residual near the singular point, exact heat exterior, and inner swirl growth; proved by Proposition 9.9 and consumed by Section 10 (Prop 10.1, Lemma 10.2, proof of Theorem 1.1).

hypotheses: A leading field (velocity and pressure) on t < 1, or a scalar auxiliary profile in the similarity variables (X, eta)
preamble_entries.conclusion: A leading field is regular at the axis if its velocity and pressure extend smoothly across r = 0 in Cartesian coordinates for t < 1. For scalar auxiliary profiles, regular at the axis means a smooth extension in (X, eta) to X = 0.
preamble_entries.role: Fixes what axis regularity means for the profiles and fields, used whenever smoothness of the construction at r = 0 is asserted (e.g. Theorem 3.1(i), Prop 9.9 Step 2, Prop 10.1).

hypotheses: alpha >= 0 and beta > 0 are parameters in the construction
preamble_entries.conclusion: alpha << beta means alpha/beta is required to be sufficiently small, with the allowed size depending on all data already fixed. In a chain of constants, choices proceed from right to left; small reciprocals specify large parameters. For expressions depending on profile variables, this smallness is uniform on the stated domain and is ensured by those parameter choices.
preamble_entries.role: Convention for the order in which smallness parameters are chosen throughout the paper.

hypotheses: A fixed wave label, a harmonic index m in Z \ {0}, and an exponent alpha in R
Source amplitude f_m in W_alpha satisfying the support and smooth-extension hypotheses of Proposition 7.2
The source harmonic f_m e^{i k m Phi} extends smoothly by zero outside the fixed local rectangle, including its pulse endpoints
(t_m, pi_m) solves the principal amplitude-pressure equation L_m(t_m, pi_m) = -f_m of (9.1) with n_Phi . t_m = 0 (alternatively, t_m in W_alpha is a homogeneous pulse with f_m = 0)
The potential (7.38) and the pressure are multiplied by the pulse cutoff and the curl is taken, giving velocity amplitude a_m = t_m + r_m with curl correction r_m
entries.conclusion: The normalized linear residual of this curl-generated harmonic, after adding the prescribed source f_m e^{ikmPhi}, belongs to W_{alpha + 1/2 - 3 kappa_s}, apart from additive pulse-cutoff tails whose Cartesian space-time derivatives vanish to infinite order as q -> 0. The pressure amplitude pi_m belongs to W_{alpha + 1/2}.
constants: kappa_s = 10^{-5} (fixed for all of Section 9)
L_m(a, pi) = Q^{1+h} N_abs a + K a + eps k^2 m^2 |n_Phi|^2 a + i k m n_Phi pi (9.1); eps = Q^h, Q = 2^{-l}, S_* = l^2
C_m = i n_Phi x t_m / (k m |n_Phi|^2), curl_*(C_m e^{ikmPhi}) = (t_m + r_m) e^{ikmPhi}; t_m in W_alpha implies r_m in W_{alpha + 1/2 - kappa_s} (Lemma 7.7)

gain table above alpha for the remainder (9.2): slow transport 1 - kappa_s; phase transport defect 1/2; base derivatives and connections 1; pressure-amplitude gradient 1/2 - kappa_s; viscous amplitude derivatives 1 - 2 kappa_s; mixed derivatives and phase divergence 1/2 - kappa_s; viscous angular connection 1/2
common lower bound alpha + 1/2 - 3 kappa_s at every derivative order
eps k^2 = O(1)
cutoff tails supported where P_v <= e^{-c S_*}; each fixed derivative bounded by C Q^{-M} S_*^P e^{-c S_*}, flat since S_* = l^2 and Q = 2^{-l}
entries.role: Quantifies the gain (1/2 - 3 kappa_s) of the linear residual left after one forward pulse solve, used in Step 1 and Step 2 of the correction cycle (Prop 9.6) and in Prop 9.3.

hypotheses: w is a wave in W_alpha
v is a mean field with tangential components in M_mu and radial component in M_{mu+1}
For the second part: w, w' are two curl-generated waves with the same label and exponents alpha, alpha'
(w . grad_*) v denotes cylindrical transport with normalized derivatives (D_r, R^{-1} d_theta, D_z) including differentiation of the cylindrical frame
entries.conclusion: The nonzero harmonics of (w . grad_*) v + (v . grad_*) w belong to W_{alpha + mu - 1/2}. For two curl-generated waves w, w' with the same label, the nonzero harmonics of (w . grad_*) w' + (w' . grad_*) w belong to W_{alpha + alpha' - kappa_s} and the zero harmonic belongs to the mean class M_{alpha + alpha' - kappa_s}. Waves with distinct labels have zero products on their closed supports.
constants: mean advection of a wave phase costs k = O(eps^{-1/2}) (the 1/2 loss)
wave transport of a mean costs at most kappa_s radially
product weights: P_v^2 <= P_v and radial weight zeta (stronger than the required sqrt(zeta))
phase differentiation gives i k m' (a . n_Phi) a'; (7.39) cancels the apparent half-power loss
entries.role: Bounds the nonlinear wave-mean and wave-wave interaction terms created by each increment, supplying rows of the exponent tables in Props 9.5 and 9.6.

hypotheses: j in N_0 is a fixed stage

(u^[j], p^[j]) is obtained from the fixed slow base and primary waves by a finite sequence of: the pulse inverse and curl construction, the signed amplitude map for auxiliary-independent stresses, and the mean maps of Section 8
Pressure is reconstructed by (8.12) after each update
All products use the complete velocity fields
entries.conclusion: There is a physical residual decomposition R(u^[j], p^[j]) = G^[j] + F^[j] (9.3); with G^[j]_* = Q^{2A+1/2} G^[j], F^[j]_* = Q^{2A+1/2} F^[j] in a common chart: (i) Supported sources: on the coarsest common auxiliary torus the nonzero angular harmonics have the form G^[j]_* - <G^[j]_*>_theta = sum_{gamma in Gamma} sum_{m in H_j} f^[j]_{gamma,m} e^{i k_gamma m Phi_gamma} (9.4), H_j subset Z \ {0} finite and independent of band, the sum locally finite; supp(f^[j]_{gamma,m}|E_gamma) subset Omega_gamma, f^[j]_{gamma,m} in C^infty(E^+_gamma; C^3) with smooth zero extension across the fixed slow and transverse supports and the enlarged local torus rectangle; if alpha, mu are any lower bounds for the wave and mean exponents furnished by Props 9.1, 7.2, 6.6, 7.6, Section 8 and Lemma 9.2 along the sequence, then f^[j]_{gamma,m} in W_alpha and <G^[j]_*>_theta in M_mu, with smooth zero extension of the mean coefficients outside the active shell; the next pulse inverse is applied precisely to the f^[j]_{gamma,m}. (ii) Flat remainder: for every fixed j, m, N, |F^[j]|_m <= C_{j,m,N} q^N (9.5), uniformly over bands, labels and points. (iii) Exact mean equations (9.6): with the complete current correction (beta^[j], v^[j], gamma^[j], w^[j]) and E_{B,*} = Q^{2A+1/2} E_B, W^[j]_{ab} = <w^[j]_a w^[j]_b>_theta, P^[j] = int <g^[j]_r>_Y dR, p^[j]_m = T_0(g^[j]_r - rho P^[j]), and <G^[j]_* + F^[j]_* - E_{B,*}>_theta = (D_r p^[j]_m - g^[j]_r, E^[j]_theta, E^[j]_z) with g_r, E_theta, E_z given by (8.3) on this tuple.
constants: normalization G_* = Q^{2A+1/2} G, F_* = Q^{2A+1/2} F, E_{B,*} = Q^{2A+1/2} E_B
an explicit D_r costs kappa_s each time it occurs
edge weight zeta = e^{-a/s^2} times a smooth positive bounded factor, a > 0 fixed, s the logarithmic edge distance of (6.23)
int_0^delta s^{-M} e^{-a/s^2} ds <= C_{M,a} delta^{3-M} e^{-a/delta^2} and |d^k/ds^k e^{-a/s^2}| <= C_{k,a} s^{-3k} e^{-a/s^2}
amplitude division as in (7.31): d Sigma = H^{-1}(Sigma/eps), delta a_sigma = (d Sigma)_sigma / (2 a_sigma)

|D^I (d Sigma)_sigma| <= C eps^{alpha-1} S_*^b zeta delta^{-M}; |D^I (a_sigma^{-1})| <= C S_*^b zeta^{-1/2} delta^{-M}; |D^I delta a_sigma| <= C eps^{alpha-1} S_*^b sqrt(zeta) delta^{-M}; |D^I (sqrt(eps) delta a_sigma b_sigma)| <= C eps^{alpha-1/2} S_*^b sqrt(zeta) delta^{-M} P_v (recovers (7.33); after slow cutoff this is the W_{alpha-1/2} estimate of Prop 7.6)
a radial mean can aggregate polynomially many labels in S_*; only boundedly many wave labels overlap at a point
entries.role: Bookkeeping proposition guaranteeing that after any finite sequence of corrections the residual splits into supported sources (satisfying the hypotheses of the pulse inverse for the next cycle) plus a flat remainder, and that the exact mean balances hold; it feeds Definition 9.4 and closes the induction in Prop 9.6.

hypotheses: j in N union {0}

Real fields of the normalized form (9.7): u_* = (b + beta, V + v, G + gamma) + w, p_* = p_{B,*} + p_m + p_w, <w>_theta = <p_w>_theta = 0, with base (b, V, G), base pressure p_{B,*}, p_w the pressure harmonics from the amplitude equations, and p_m reconstructed from the current g_r by (8.12)

The wave w is a sum of curls of supported wave potentials with the fixed label phases; the mean correction (beta, v, gamma) is the sum of a curl of an azimuthal potential and a direct azimuthal field (so both corrections are exactly divergence-free)
Source supports, finite harmonic sets, smooth zero extensions and the physical residual decomposition are as in Proposition 9.3
entries.conclusion: Such fields form a state at stage j when: (9.8) the normalized nonzero harmonics G^[j]_wave of G^[j]_* lie in W_{B_j}, the exact tangential mean residuals E_theta, E_z lie in M_{C*_j}, and the three integral defects (P, J_theta, J_z) lie in S_{C*_j}, with B_j = 1/2 + sigma_j, C*_j = 1 + sigma_j, sigma_j = 1/5 + j/10; (9.9) the total corrections satisfy w in W_{1/2}, w - w_0^tan in W_{0.68}, v, gamma, p_m in M_{0.9}, beta in M_{1.9} (wave assertions per grouped nonzero harmonic per label); (9.10) the normalized angular-momentum and axial-flux moments int_0^infty R^2 <v>_Y dR = 0 and int_0^infty R <gamma>_Y dR = 0 hold exactly; and the pressure reconstruction is part of the state. Consequently the radial residual of every state is -rho P plus the flat cutoff remainder of Proposition 8.3.
constants: B_j = 1/2 + sigma_j, C*_j = 1 + sigma_j, sigma_j = 1/5 + j/10
cumulative bounds: w in W_{1/2}, w - w_0^tan in W_{0.68}, v, gamma, p_m in M_{0.9}, beta in M_{1.9}
moment constraints int R^2 <v>_Y dR = 0, int R <gamma>_Y dR = 0
w_0^tan = W^as_0 is the normalized assembled primary transverse field of (7.35)
entries.role: The induction hypothesis of the correction cycle: it records the residual orders and cumulative velocity bounds that Prop 9.5 initializes and Prop 9.6 improves by 1/10 per cycle.

hypotheses: Start from the fixed base (b, V, G) and the curls of the primary potentials (the primary pulses of Prop 7.5 assembled by (7.35), made divergence-free by Lemma 7.7)
Perform the temporal mean update (8.20) and then the five-equation correction (8.25)
Reconstruct the pressure by (8.12) before and after each update
entries.conclusion: The resulting fields form a state at stage 0 in the sense of Definition 9.4; in particular their residual orders are B_0 = 0.7 and C*_0 = 1.2, the cumulative bounds (9.9) hold, and the moments (9.10) are enforced.
constants: primary transverse amplitudes have exponent 1/2; their supported linear residual has exponent 1 - 3 kappa_s; nonlinear wave residuals 1 - kappa_s
before any mean update: g_r, p_m, E_theta, E_z in M_{1 - kappa_s}, defects in S_{1 - kappa_s}

curl-correction x primary-transverse cross tensor in M_{3/2 - kappa_s}; axial fluxes, axial pressure term and higher-order auxiliary stress tensor have residual exponent >= 2 - kappa_s; hence <E_theta>_Y, <E_z>_Y in M_{1.49}
H_0 = 1 - kappa_s: temporal update increments in M_{H_0} (tangential) and M_{H_0 + 1} (induced radial); pressure change exponent H_0 (from 2 V Delta v / R in Delta g_r)
residual changes from the temporal update have exponent >= H_0 + 1 - 2 kappa_s; viscosity gains 1 - 2 kappa_s; mean interaction with w in W_{1/2} has wave exponent >= H_0
five-equation map at order H_0: other terms gain > 0.8 above H_0; remaining defects exponent > 1.8 - kappa_s; tangential means retain 1.49
primary curl correction exponent 1 - kappa_s > 0.68; mean increments H_0 > 0.9; radial H_0 + 1 > 1.9
entries.role: Initializes the correction induction: shows the primary pulses plus one round of mean corrections already satisfy the stage-0 state bounds, with the primary covariance of Prop 7.5 cancelling the order-zero auxiliary stress exactly via (9.11).

hypotheses: (u^[j], p^[j]) is a state at stage j in the sense of Definition 9.4 (so (9.8) with B_j, C*_j, (9.9), (9.10) hold)
The same base (b, V, G), primary amplitudes, supports and inverse operators are used throughout

The four corrections are applied in order: (i) solve the inhomogeneous amplitude equation for each supported nonzero harmonic; (ii) change the wave amplitudes to correct the auxiliary-averaged tangential residual; (iii) apply the temporal mean inverse to the part with zero auxiliary average; (iv) apply the five-equation correction to the three current defects; pressure reconstructed after each correction
Wave and meridional velocity increments are realized by their potentials; azimuthal mean increments are added directly
entries.conclusion: There is a state (u^[j+1], p^[j+1]) at stage j+1, constructed as described, whose residual orders are B_{j+1} = B_j + 1/10 and C*_{j+1} = C*_j + 1/10. The cumulative bounds (9.9) and the exact moments (9.10) are preserved, and the radial residual is again -rho P plus the flat remainder.
constants: abbreviations B = 1/2 + sigma_j, C* = B + 1/2 = 1 + sigma_j; used B >= 0.7
pressure update after each step: P_new = int <g_{r,new}>_Y dR, p_{m,new} = T_0(g_{r,new} - rho P_new)
Step 1 increments: Delta w_m = curl_*((i n_Phi x (psi t_m))/(k m |n_Phi|^2) e^{ikmPhi}), Delta p_{w,m} = psi pi_m e^{ikmPhi}, L_m(t_m, pi_m) = -f_m; velocity in W_B, pressure in W_{B+1/2}
Step 1 nonzero-harmonic errors: linear B + 1/2 - 3 kappa_s; cross with old exact waves B + 1/2 - kappa_s; particular-correction self-interaction 2B - kappa_s; cross with total mean correction B + 0.4

Step 1 means: covariance changes exponent >= B + 1/2 = C*; radial divergence costs kappa_s; E_theta, E_z, Delta g_r, Delta p_m in M_{C* - kappa_s}; (P, J_theta, J_z) in S_{C* - kappa_s}; weighted moments int R^2 <E_theta>_Y dR, int R <E_z>_Y dR in S_{C* + 1 - kappa_s} (9.12)

Step 2: F_2 = Q^{-2A-1/2} <E_theta>_Y, F_1 = Q^{-2A-1/2} <E_z>_Y; fixed interior profile hat b_e with int x^e hat b_e dx = 1, b_e(r,z,t) = q^{-(e+1)/2} hat b_e(r/sqrt(q)); M_e = int_0^infty r^e F_e dr; sigma_e(r) = -r^{-e} int_0^r (r')^e (F_e - b_e M_e) dr'; (d_r + e/r) sigma_e = -F_e + b_e M_e; Sigma = Q^{2A}(sigma_2, sigma_1) in M_{C* - kappa_s}
Step 2: L^as Sigma in W_{B - kappa_s} with prescribed symmetrized cross covariance Sigma with w_0^tan; division by the fixed positive primary amplitude 2 sqrt(y_sigma)
Step 2 nonzero-harmonic errors: linear B + 1/2 - 4 kappa_s; mean interaction B + 0.4 - kappa_s; cross with old exact waves B + 1/2 - 2 kappa_s; signed-correction self-interaction 2B - 3 kappa_s

Step 2 covariance expansion (9.13): <Delta W>_Y = B(w_0^tan, t_s) + B(w - w_0^tan, t_s) + B(w, r_s) + <<s (x) s>_theta>_Y, s = t_s + r_s; remainder exponents before divergence: B + 0.68 - kappa_s = C* + 0.18 - kappa_s; C* + 1/2 - 2 kappa_s; 2B - 2 kappa_s = C* + sigma_j - 2 kappa_s; b_e M_e term of order C* + 1 - kappa_s
(9.14): <E_theta>_Y, <E_z>_Y in M_{C* + 0.17}; E_theta, E_z in M_H; (P, J_theta, J_z) in S_H; H = C* - 2 kappa_s (using 0.18 - 2 kappa_s > 0.17 and sigma_j - 3 kappa_s > 0.17)

Step 3: E^o_a = E_a - <E_a>_Y; Delta v = -c_{i0}^{-1} N_{i0}^{-1} E^o_theta, gamma_d = -c_{i0}^{-1} N_{i0}^{-1} E^o_z, Psi_* = T_1 gamma_d, Delta beta = -eps d_Z Psi_*, Delta gamma = (D_r + R^{-1}) Psi_*; t_* = -eps d_T + c_{i0} N_{i0}; fast-time identities c N Delta v = -E^o_theta, c N Delta gamma = -E^o_z + F_ax, F_ax = c N (Delta gamma - gamma_d) flat

Step 3 term exponents: slow time H + 1; radial flux H + 1 - kappa_s; axial flux H + 1; viscosity H + 1 - 2 kappa_s; |D^I b| <= C eps S_*^b on the shell; result E_theta, E_z in M_{min(C* + 0.17, H + 1 - 2 kappa_s)}, defects S_H, wave change in W_H

Step 4: five-equation map at order H; increments in M_H (tangential), M_{H+1} (radial); remainder exponent >= H + 0.9 - 2 kappa_s; (P, J_theta, J_z) in S_{H + 0.9 - 2 kappa_s} = S_{C* + 0.9 - 4 kappa_s}

closing inequalities: min{1/2 - 3 kappa_s, 1/2 - kappa_s, B - kappa_s, 0.4} >= 0.4; min{1/2 - 4 kappa_s, 0.4 - kappa_s, 1/2 - 2 kappa_s, B - 3 kappa_s} >= 0.4 - kappa_s; H - B = 1/2 - 2 kappa_s > 0.1; min{0.17, 1 - 4 kappa_s} = 0.17 > 0.1; 0.9 - 4 kappa_s > 0.1
smallest signed increment order B - kappa_s >= 0.69999 > 0.68; particular increments start at B >= 0.7; mean increments > 0.9; radial mean increments > 1.9
entries.role: The inductive step: one full four-operation correction cycle raises every residual order by 1/10 while preserving the cumulative velocity bounds and the two moment constraints, so the cycle can be iterated indefinitely.

hypotheses: The finite partial sums (u^[j], p^[j]) of the correction cycle, before applying summation cutoffs, built with the fixed background, the fixed positive lower bound for |n_Phi|, the primary covariance, and the fixed supports of the normalized mean-correction profiles
All later inhomogeneous amplitude problems are linear equations with these fixed coefficients and known sources
entries.conclusion: There exists q_big > 0, independent of the correction stage and derivative order, such that every finite partial sum, before summation cutoffs, is well defined on 0 < q < q_big. For every fixed stage and output amplitude derivative, the construction and its estimate require only finitely many input amplitude derivatives. The constants may depend on the correction stage.
constants: 0 < q_big <= q_*, chosen once so that the pulse estimates hold for q < q_big
propagator of each harmonic = fundamental propagator times a forward damping factor of magnitude at most one (7.18)
signed updates divide by the original 2 sqrt(y_sigma) of (7.31)
derivative-count recursion on the DAG of operations: D_{v,a}(m) = max_{w -> v} D_{w,a}(m + d_{v,w}), with D_{b,a}(m) = m if b = a and 0 otherwise
entries.role: Provides the single common domain on which all finite correction stages live and finiteness of derivative requirements, a hypothesis for the summation lemma (Lemma 5.4) used in Prop 9.9.

hypotheses: The stage tuples Z_j = (A_j, B_j, p_j) and increments Delta u_j = curl A_j + B_j = u^[j] - u^[j-1] of (9.15), with p_j given by (9.16), for j >= 1; U_0 = (u^[0], p^[0]) the base plus finite initialization
Cartesian space-time jet norms |.|_m of (5.23); perturbation supports have r ~ sqrt(Q), q ~ Q, and Q is held fixed while differentiating in a chart
entries.conclusion: (9.17): for every m, |Z_j|_m + |Delta u_j|_m <= C_{j,m} q^{g_j - l_m} (1 + |log q|)^{P_{j,m}} with g_j = h j/10 -> infty and l_m independent of j (l_m includes the extra spatial derivative recovering velocities from wave and mean vector potentials). The finite partial sums satisfy |(u^[j], p^[j])|_m <= C_{j,m} q^{-K_m} (1 + |log q|)^{P_{j,m}} with K_m independent of j. Their residuals satisfy (9.18): |R(u^[j], p^[j])|_m <= C_{j,m} q^{h sigma_j - K_m} (1 + |log q|)^{P_{j,m}} + E_{j,m}, with E_{j,m} <= C_{j,m,N} q^N for every N and K_m independent of j.
constants: g_j = h j / 10 (stage-j increment has normalized exponent >= j/10)
(9.19) Q-power losses per physical derivative of an amplitude coefficient: radial 1/2 + h kappa_s; axial D = 1/2 - h; time 1 + h; cylindrical frame derivative 1/2
r d_r^{-1} Lambda_{i0} g = O(Q^{-1/2} eps^{-kappa_s} S_*^P); T_{i0} g = O(Q^{-1-h} S_*^P)
|grad_x Phi| <= C Q^{-1/2} S_*^P, |d_t Phi| <= C Q^{-1-h} S_*^P; axial term p_z Z/eps costs Q^{-D} eps^{-1} = Q^{-1/2}; |grad^a d_t^b Phi_gamma| <= C Q^{-a/2 - b(1+h)} S_*^P for a + b >= 1
s_x = 1/2 + h/2, s_t = 1 + 3h/2; k <= 2 Q^{-h/2}; |grad^a d_t^b e^{ikmPhi}| <= C Q^{-a s_x - b s_t} S_*^P

hard_pages.why: Proof of Proposition 9.6: four steps each with its own exponent table, and the closing inequalities on p. 111 must be checked against every row. Specific points: the Step 1 row 'cross with total mean correction B + 0.4' relies on Lemma 9.2 with mu = 0.9 from (9.9) (alpha + mu - 1/2); Step 2's covariance remainder 'B + 0.68 - kappa_s = C* + 0.18 - kappa_s' uses the w - w_0^tan in W_{0.68} bound and is what fixes the 0.17 in (9.14); Step 3's claim that all four term types reach H + 1 - 2 kappa_s depends on |D^I b| <= C eps S_*^b for the base radial velocity; and the final 'H - B = 1/2 - 2 kappa_s > 0.1' is the only place the wave improvement from Step 3 is checked. The definition of L^as_phys and the covariance identity (7.36) are invoked without restatement.

Proof of Proposition 9.3(i): the weighted radial-integral estimate uses zeta = e^{-a/s^2} with the bounds int_0^delta s^{-M} e^{-a/s^2} ds <= C delta^{3-M} e^{-a/delta^2} and |d^k/ds^k e^{-a/s^2}| <= C s^{-3k} e^{-a/s^2}, and then the amplitude-division bounds (|D^I delta a_sigma| etc.) that 'recover (7.33)'; verifying that the sqrt(zeta) weight survives division by a_sigma^{-1} ~ zeta^{-1/2} requires Section 7 material (7.25), (7.31), (7.33) not in this shard.

Lemma 9.8: the loss table (9.19) (radial 1/2 + h kappa_s, axial D, time 1 + h, frame 1/2) and the phase-derivative bounds leading to s_x = 1/2 + h/2, s_t = 1 + 3h/2 and l_m = 2A + (m+1)(1 + 3h/2); the extracted text of (9.17) is garbled ('gj = 10h ... j -> infty'), and g_j = h j/10 had to be recovered from p. 114 Step 1 of Prop 9.9.

Lemma 10.5 pressure flux: the commutator kernel K_R = C|x-y|^{-3} min{|x-y|/R, 1} and the computation ||K_R||_{4/3}^{4/3} <= C R^{-1} (inner integral R^{-4/3} int_0^R r^{-2/3} dr = 3 R^{-1}, outer int_R^infty r^{-2} dr = R^{-1}), then the Young/Holder pairing giving the R^{-1} R^{-3/4} B_R^{3/4} term in (10.19) and the check that every power of A_R is <= 3/2 so Young's inequality absorbs into A_R^2. Also the identification grad pi = grad pi_* via H_a in H^{-3} with Fourier support at {0}.

Prop 9.9 Step 4: the bound sup |H_ext^{(m)}| <= 2A c_infty 4^m (h)_m (1+h)_m comes from the integral (A.34) in Appendix A, and the identification H_ext(s) = 2A c_infty H(4s) with the exterior formula (4.29) cannot be checked from this shard's pages.

could_not_determine.why: The extracted statement of (9.17) reads 'gj = 10h' with a dangling 'j -> infty', so the exact printed form of g_j in the lemma is garbled; I recorded g_j = h j/10 based on p. 114 ('Lemma 9.8 supplies (5.30) with gj = hj/10') and the proof's 'stage-j increment has normalized exponent at least j/10'.
The theorem is a pure existence statement with no hypotheses beyond the fixed choices of Sections 4-9; I recorded only the constants it introduces and the coordinate conventions it assumes.

Step 2 invokes the operator L^as_phys 'from (7.35)' and the covariance identity (7.36) and the amplitude formula (7.31); I recorded these labels as cited but could not verify from pages 100-126 that (7.35) defines L^as_phys rather than only W^as_0.
